definitions.explanation: A building or hall where religious ceremonies, rituals, or festivals are conducted. Used for both Shinto and Buddhist contexts, as well as more broadly for any sacred or ceremonial space.

examples.japanese: {祭殿|さいでん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{神事|しんじ}→神事：14066_shinji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: A Shinto ritual was performed in the ceremonial hall.

examples.japanese: {祭殿|さいでん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参拝者|さんぱいしゃ}→参拝者：21620_sanpaisha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: Worshippers are lined up in front of the ceremonial hall.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古代|こだい}→古代：05324_kodai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{祭殿|さいでん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{跡|あと}→跡：02174_ato⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発掘|はっくつ}→発掘：07995_hakkutsu⟧⟦{調査|ちょうさ}→調査：03489_chousa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{発見|はっけん}→発見：00085_hakken⟧⟦され→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{当時|とうじ}→当時：01615_touji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{祭祀|さいし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{様子|ようす}→様子：01521_yousu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}る→知る：00458_shiru⟧{手|て}がかり⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The remains of an ancient ceremonial hall were discovered in an excavation, providing clues about the rituals of the time.

notes:
A compound of {祭|さい} (festival/ritual) and {殿|でん} (hall/palace). Refers to a building or space specifically designated for conducting religious ceremonies or rituals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祭殿|さいでん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{祀|まつ}る: enshrine in a ceremonial hall
- {祭殿|さいでん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧: build a ceremonial hall
- {祭殿|さいでん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧: inside the ceremonial hall

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{拝殿|はいでん}→拝殿：24252_haiden⟧: worship hall (the hall in front of a shrine where visitors pray)
- ⟦{本殿|ほんでん}→本殿：13090_honden⟧: main hall (the innermost building of a shrine housing the deity)
- ⟦{神殿|しんでん}→神殿：18822_shinden⟧: divine hall; temple (hall where a deity is enshrined)
- ⟦{社殿|しゃでん}→社殿：20755_shaden⟧: shrine buildings (collective term for the buildings of a Shinto shrine)
